_meta.title: Method presets for UV-Vis quantification of secondary metabolites
_meta.note: Values taken from the literature listed in 'references'. Items whose 'source' is 'general_knowledge' are standard analytical practice not taken from those references: verify them against your laboratory protocol before using them in production. Molar masses of the reference standards are general reference values (general_knowledge).
_meta.how_to_edit: Add or edit methods here; the app reads this file at start-up. Each value should state its 'source' ('literature' or 'general_knowledge').

acceptance.recovery_source: AOAC criterion for complex matrices cited by Ruiz-Vásquez et al. (2026); 98–102% is usual in pharmaceutical analysis

methods.name: Generic Beer-Lambert calibration
methods.principle: Any analyte (or coloured derivative) whose absorbance follows A = ε·l·c.

methods.name: Total phenolics – Folin-Ciocalteu
methods.analyte: Total phenolic content (reducing compounds, mainly phenolics)
methods.principle: Reduction of the phosphomolybdate–phosphotungstate complex in alkaline medium (Na2CO3) to a blue complex.
warnings: Not specific: reducing sugars, ascorbic acid, proteins and other reductants interfere.
The order of addition matters: making the medium alkaline before adding the reagent can cause condensation and bias (Chen et al. 2015).
The result depends on the chosen standard; always report it.

methods.name: Total flavonoids – aluminium chloride
methods.analyte: Flavones and flavonols (Al3+ complex with keto and ortho-dihydroxy groups)
methods.principle: Formation of a coloured Al3+ chelate with flavonoid keto/ortho-dihydroxy groups.

variants.name: AlCl3 5% in 80% ethanol, 25 min, direct dilution, 408 nm (Ramos 2017)
AlCl3 5% in 80% ethanol, 25 min, after acid hydrolysis, 425 nm (Ramos 2017)
NaNO2–AlCl3–NaOH, 510 nm (usual standard: catechin)
variants.note: Also responds to flavan-3-ols and o-diphenols.

warnings: Different flavonoids have different λmax and absorptivity with AlCl3; the method is not universal (Mammen & Daniel 2012).
Expressing results as quercetin vs rutin changes the result greatly; recoveries can be unacceptable depending on the standard (Shraim et al. 2021).
Kaempferol and dihydrochalcones give low slopes (Matić 2017, 2021).

methods.name: Condensed tannins – vanillin-HCl
methods.principle: Condensation of vanillin with the meta-substituted A ring of flavan-3-ols in acid medium.
warnings: No single assay quantifies 'total tannins' in every matrix; combine assays (Nastasi 2025).

methods.name: Total alkaloids – bromocresol green (BCG)
methods.principle: Yellow alkaloid–BCG ion-pair complex at pH 4.7, extracted with chloroform.
methods.reported_performance: Linear 2–10 µg/mL at 415 nm; RSD < 2%; LOD 0.215, LOQ 0.652 (Tinospora cordifolia, 2015).

methods.name: Total saponins – vanillin-sulfuric acid
methods.principle: Coloured product of saponin aglycones with vanillin in concentrated sulfuric acid.

variants.name: p-Anisaldehyde-H2SO4 (Le Bot et al. 2022) – set λ from the reference
variants.note: Similar absorptivity for triterpenoid and steroidal saponins.

warnings: Acetone, methanol and n-butanol darken the reaction even without saponins; evaporate the solvent before the reaction (Le et al. 2018).
The curve changes with the solvent of the standard.

methods.name: Total monomeric anthocyanins – pH differential (AOAC 2005.02)
methods.principle: Anthocyanins are coloured (flavylium cation) at pH 1.0 and almost colourless (hemiketal) at pH 4.5. No calibration curve: uses a known ε.
methods.reported_performance: RSDr 1.06–4.16%; RSDR 2.69–10.12% (collaborative study, Lee et al. 2005).
